title: Bench top CUT&RUN with antibodies-online™ CUT&RUN Sets
author: Antibodies Online Gmbh
materials: Gently resuspend the antibodies-online™ CUT&RUN Concanavalin A Beads antibodies-online Catalog #ABIN6923139

The antibodies-online™ CUT&RUN Secondary antibodies-online Catalog #ABIN6923141 is raised in rabbit against mouse IgG (H&L). In case a primary antibody from a different host species or isotype is used a different secondary must be selected accordingly. Place the tubes on a magnet stand until the fluid is clear. Remove the liquid carefully.

Add 1 µL antibodies-online™ CUT&RUN Secondary antibodies-online Catalog #ABIN6923141 corresponding to a 1:100 dilution (or a volume corresponding to the manufacturer’s recommended dilution for immunofluorescence).
Optional: Transfer liquid to a phase-lock tube.

Size distribution and concentration of the CUT&RUN products can be assessed at this point, e.g. using a Qubit (Flurometer, Invitrogen, Q33228, https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/Q33228 , https://s3.amazonaws.com/pr-journal/9de3sqe.jpeg ) or NanoDrop™ 3300 Fluorospectrometer (Fluorospectrometer, NanoDrop™ 3300, nd-3300, https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/ND-3300#/ND-3300 , https://s3.amazonaws.com/protocols-files/public/0a4fe9b7a11f73c8ba5166c11a7060d8420e56909f0bef279aef656fabd5f2ab/btsr9xr6.jpg ) or a Bioanalyzer or Tapestation. It is possible that the concentration of the recovered DNA is below the instrument’s detection limit. It is also to be expected that the extracted DNA includes some large DNA fragments that will mask the signal of the CUT&RUN products. In this case it may be useful to PCR-amplify the DNA and check the library on a Bioanalyzer or Tapestation.

steps.title: Prepare Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 156.7 mL ddH₂O, 3.3 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5 (final 20 mM), 4.95 mL 5 M NaCl (final 150 mM), and 41.25 µL 2 M Spermidine (final 0.5 mM) to a total volume of 165 mL. Store at 4 °C for up to one week; add protease inhibitors fresh before use (e.g., 1.65 mL EDTA‑free inhibitor).

steps.title: Prepare Binding Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 43.6 mL ddH₂O, 900 µL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5 (20 mM), 450 µL 1 M KCl (10 mM), 45 µL 1 M CaCl₂ (1 mM), and 16 µL 2.5 M MnCl₂ (1 mM) to a final volume of 45 mL. Store at 4 °C for up to six months.

steps.title: Prepare Digitonin Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 3 354 µL 1.2 % Digitonin (final 0.05 %) to 79 mL Wash Buffer to make 82.5 mL total. Store at 4 °C for up to one day. Test cell permeability with Trypan Blue to adjust Digitonin (0.025‑0.1 %).

steps.title: Prepare Antibody Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 6 µL 0.5 M EDTA (final 2 mM), 15 µL 10 % BSA (final 0.1 %), and 1.5 mL Digitonin Wash Buffer to 1.5 mL total. Store at 4 °C for up to one day.

steps.title: Prepare Low Salt Rinse Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 25.3 mL ddH₂O, 540 µL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5 (20 mM), 6.75 µL 2 M Spermidine (0.5 mM), and 1 125 µL 1.2 % Digitonin (0.05 %) to 27 mL total. Store at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare Low Salt Incubation Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 2.8 mL ddH₂O, 10.5 µL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5 (3.5 mM), 30 µL 1 M CaCl₂ (10 mM), and 125 µL 1.2 % Digitonin (0.05 %) to 3 mL total. Store at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare Low Salt Stop Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 2.8 mL ddH₂O, 102 µL 5 M NaCl (170 mM), and 300 µL 0.2 M EGTA (20 mM) to 3 mL total. Store at 4 °C; add fresh before use: 125 µL 1.2 % Digitonin (0.05 %), 15 µL RNase A (10 mg/mL, final 50 µg/mL), 7.5 µL Glycogen (20 mg/mL, final 25 µg/mL), and optionally heterologous spike‑in DNA to 100 pg/mL.

steps.title: Harvest Cells
steps.instruction: Collect 10 000–500 000 cells per sample at room temperature and keep each sample in a separate tube.

steps.title: First Wash of Cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cell suspension 3 min at 600 × g, room temperature; carefully remove supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend in Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Gently pipette to resuspend cells in 1 mL Wash Buffer and transfer to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Second Wash of Cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 3 min at 600 × g, room temperature; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Repeat Cell Washes
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash (steps 9‑11) two more times for a total of four washes.

steps.title: Resuspend Pellet After Final Wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 1 mL Wash Buffer by gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Add Concanavalin A Beads
steps.instruction: Pipette 10 µL CUT&RUN Concanavalin A bead slurry into each tube.

steps.title: Capture Beads on Magnet
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic stand until the liquid clears; carefully remove supernatant.

steps.title: Wash Beads with Binding Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL Binding Buffer, gently resuspend beads, then spin the lid briefly (≤100 × g). Place on magnet and remove liquid.

steps.title: Repeat Bead Washes
steps.instruction: Repeat the bead‑wash (steps 14‑16) two additional times for a total of three washes.

steps.title: Resuspend Beads in Binding Buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the Concanavalin A beads in Binding Buffer equal to the original bead slurry volume (10 µL per sample).

steps.title: Combine Cells and Beads
steps.instruction: Vortex the cell suspension, then add 10 µL of the bead suspension to each sample.

steps.title: Incubate Cells with Beads
steps.instruction: Close tubes tightly and rotate for 5–10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Remove Unbound Material
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnet until clear; remove supernatant.

steps.title: Add Antibody Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL Antibody Buffer (contains digitonin) to each tube and vortex gently to resuspend beads.

steps.title: Add Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL primary rabbit antibody (1:100 dilution or manufacturer‑recommended dilution) to each tube.

steps.title: Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Rotate tubes for 5–10 min at room temperature, or 2 h at room temperature up to overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash After Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Spin down briefly, place on magnet, and remove supernatant.

steps.title: Digitonin Wash #1
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL Digitonin Wash Buffer, invert to mix; if clumps form, remove with a 1 mL pipette tip.

steps.title: Repeat Digitonin Wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the Digitonin Wash (previous step) once for a total of two washes. If no secondary antibody is used, proceed to pA/G‑MNase binding.

steps.title: Low‑Speed Vortex and Wash
steps.instruction: Place tubes at a low angle on a vortex mixer (~1100 rpm), add 100 µL Digitonin Wash Buffer along the tube side, tap to release beads.

steps.title: Incubate on Ice
steps.instruction: Rotate tubes for 1 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Spin down briefly, place on magnet, and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Second Low‑Speed Wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend in 1 mL Digitonin Wash Buffer, invert; remove clumps if needed.

steps.title: Repeat Low‑Speed Wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the low‑speed wash (previous two steps) once for a total of two washes.

steps.title: Add pA/G‑MNase
steps.instruction: Place tubes on magnet, remove liquid, then add 50 µL Digitonin Wash Buffer plus 2.5 µL CUTANA™ pA/G‑MNase (catalog #ABIN6950951). Alternatively, add 150 µL Digitonin Wash Buffer containing 700 ng/mL of your own pA/G‑MNase.

steps.title: pA/G‑MNase Binding
steps.instruction: Rotate tubes for 1 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Post‑Binding Wash
steps.instruction: Spin down, place on magnet, and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Digitonin Wash After MNase
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL Digitonin Wash Buffer, invert; remove clumps if present.

steps.title: Repeat MNase Wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash (previous step) once for a total of two washes.

steps.title: Low Salt Rinse Wash #1
steps.instruction: Spin down lid briefly (≤100 × g), place on magnet, and discard liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend in Low Salt Rinse
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 1 mL Low Salt Rinse Buffer, invert; remove clumps if needed.

steps.title: Low Salt Rinse Wash #2
steps.instruction: Spin down lid briefly, place on magnet, and discard liquid.

steps.title: Repeat Low Salt Rinse
steps.instruction: Repeat the Low Salt Rinse (previous three steps) once for a total of two washes.

steps.title: Low Salt Incubation
steps.instruction: Place tubes at a low angle on vortex (~1100 rpm) and add 200 µL ice‑cold Low Salt Incubation Buffer per sample.

steps.title: Incubate at 0°C
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 0 °C for the desired time (default 30 min).

steps.title: Low Salt Stop Reaction
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a cold magnet stand, remove liquid, then resuspend with 200 µL Low Salt Stop Solution and vortex gently.

steps.title: Digest Release
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Collect Digested Chromatin
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnet, allow fluid to clear, and transfer the supernatant (pA/G‑MNase‑bound fragments) to fresh 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Add SDS and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL 10 % SDS (final 0.1 %) and 5 µL Proteinase K (10 mg/mL, final 2.5 mg/mL) to each supernatant.

steps.title: Vortex After Enzyme Addition
steps.instruction: Vortex tubes at low speed (~1100 rpm).

steps.title: Proteinase K Digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate at 50 °C for 1 h or at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Phenol‑Chloroform Extraction 1
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (PCI) to each tube, vortex at high speed until milky.

steps.title: Centrifuge After PCI
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer Aqueous Phase 1
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a fresh 1.5 mL tube containing 200 µL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1).

steps.title: Phenol‑Chloroform Extraction 2
steps.instruction: Vortex at high speed until milky, then centrifuge 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer Aqueous Phase 2
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a fresh 1.5 mL tube containing 2 µL glycogen (1:10 diluted to 2 mg/mL from 20 mg/mL stock).

steps.title: Precipitation Salt Addition
steps.instruction: Add either 20 µL 3 M NaOAc or 100 µL 5 M NH₄OAc.

steps.title: Ethanol Precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 100 % ethanol, mix, and place tubes for 10 min on dry ice/ethanol or overnight at –20 °C.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, carefully remove supernatant with a pipette.

steps.title: Wash Pellet with 70% Ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min, and remove liquid.

steps.title: Dry DNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet or dry in a SpeedVac.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Dissolve the pellet in 30 µL 1 mM Tris‑HCl, 0.1 mM EDTA.

steps.title: Prepare Sequencing Libraries
steps.instruction: Construct CUT&RUN sequencing libraries using your established workflow; typically 5 million paired‑end reads are sufficient for most epitopes.

steps.title: Add Positive Control
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL CUT&Tag rabbit anti‑H3K4me3 IgG Positive Control (1:20 dilution, catalog #ABIN6923144) to the designated tube.

steps.title: Add Negative Control
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL CUT&RUN guinea‑pig anti‑rabbit IgG Negative Control (1:20 dilution, catalog #ABIN6923140) to the designated tube.

steps.title: Add DYKDDDDK Control
steps.instruction: If using CUT&RUN anti‑DYKDDDDK antibody, add 5 µL (1:20 dilution) to the appropriate tube.

description: The sparse background signal in CUT&RUN samples compared to ChIP-seq samples represents challenge for peak callers that employ statistical models relying on a high sequencing depth and high recall to identify true positives and avoid false positives. In contrast, peak calling for CUT&RUN data sets requires high specificity for true signal peaks. To this end, the Henikoff lab developed the Sparse Enrichments analysis for CUT&RUN (SEACR) peak caller that can be easily accessed using their web server at https://seacr.fredhutch.org/ . Alternatively, the Orkin and Yuan labs have streamlined processing of CUT&RUN data using their CUT&RUNTools pipeline https://bitbucket.org/qzhudfci/cutruntools/
